scholarships.title: Boren Awards (Boren Scholarships and Boren Fellowships)
scholarships.official_source: Defense Language and National Security Education Office (DLNSEO), National Security Education Program; administered by the Institute of International Education (IIE)

existing.description: The Boren Awards fund intensive overseas language study for U.S. undergraduate students (Boren Scholarships) and research or language study for U.S. graduate students (Boren Fellowships). They pay a fixed grant of $8,000, $12,500 or $25,000 depending on the duration of overseas study, and the programme states plainly that the award "is not all-inclusive" and is designed to cover only the majority of an awardee's overseas expenses. In exchange, recipients commit to at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation.
eligibility: U.S. citizens at the time of the national application deadline
A high school graduate, or have earned a GED
At least 18 years of age or older by the time the application is submitted
Planning an overseas program in an overseas destination outside of Western Europe, Canada, Australia, or New Zealand
Planning to study in an overseas destination of which they are not a citizen

Matriculated for the duration of their Boren Awards-funded program in an undergraduate or graduate degree program located within the United States and accredited by a body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education
For ROTC cadets, midshipmen and members of the military Reserves or National Guard: in inactive, non-drilling status for the duration of their Boren Awards-funded program

Boren Scholarships applicants must be matriculated in an associate's or bachelor's degree program at the time of application and must remain matriculated in an undergraduate degree program; they may not graduate until the scholarship is complete

Boren Fellowships applicants may be matriculated in or applying to a graduate degree program, but Boren Fellows must be matriculated in a graduate degree program by the start date of the fellowship and may not graduate until the fellowship is complete

Eligible graduate degree programs include master's (MA, MS, MBA, LLM and others), juris doctor (JD), or doctoral (PhD, MD and others) programs; non-degree certificate programs are not eligible by themselves
existing.eligibility_summary: U.S. citizens aged 18 or older, matriculated at an accredited U.S. undergraduate or graduate programme, proposing a continuous programme of at least 12 weeks (8 weeks for undergraduate STEM) of classroom language study in a country outside Western Europe, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, and of which they are not a citizen.
benefits: NSEP Service Team support, including resume reviews, career fairs, a mentorship program and advocacy on behalf of award recipients to human resources and hiring officials at U.S. government agencies
Access to NSEPnet, which features job listings and positions for federal government agencies exclusive to awardees
Non-competitive eligibility: until they fulfill the federal service requirement in full, Boren award recipients are eligible for non-competitive appointments to many federal positions
An annual Federal Employment Seminar in Washington, DC with training on the federal hiring process and networking with senior officials from federal agencies and contractors
Access to the NSEP Alumni Association
coverage: Home institution matriculation fees, up to $2,500/semester ($5,000 overall cap)
Fly America Act compliant round-trip airfare at the lowest cost unrestricted class (basic economy)
Cybersecurity costs including a burner laptop and/or phone, or VPN (up to $500)
One flight change fee related to approved travel and/or an approved change to program dates
Regional Flagship Language Initiative awards add the approved summer domestic cost on top of the overseas tier amount
requirements: Two letters of recommendation for Boren Scholarships (a third letter is optional); three letters of recommendation for Boren Fellowships, with at least one from a research advisor at the U.S. institution if a research component is proposed
Recommenders may be academic or professional contacts who know the applicant well; they may not be family or friends
Essay 1 - National Security, maximum 800 words, single-spaced
Essay 2 - Motivation and Public Service Careers, maximum 800 words for Boren Scholarships and 1000 words for Boren Fellowships, single-spaced
Study Plan Summary: maximum 250 words for each segment of the proposed overseas program, plus descriptions of alternate overseas destination programs
Weekly contact hours of formal language acquisition - the Boren Awards requires overseas programs contain at least 15-20 weekly language hours

An alternate study abroad program is required for applicants choosing an overseas destination marked with an asterisk (blue on the map) or for the languages Arabic, Mandarin or Russian; it is not required for Mandarin in Taiwan, Arabic in Morocco, or Language Flagship capstone applicants
Employment History: up to three jobs, each described in 50 to 100 words
Activities: up to three extracurricular activities, each described in 50 to 100 words
Language Self-Assessment in the online application, plus up to four additional languages studied or spoken
Up to three non-U.S. countries where you have lived, traveled or studied; up to five relevant honours and awards; optional list of up to five other scholarships applied for
Applicants must agree to the policies in the Submission Information section in order to actually submit
Boren Scholars whose airfare is funded by Boren must comply with the Fly America Act and send a photocopy of the passenger receipt page(s) to their airline to show compliance
All Boren-funded programs must include language study within a classroom as a core element for the duration of the grant
documents: UNOFFICIAL transcript from the current U.S. institution - required in order to submit the application
UNOFFICIAL transcripts from up to two additional institutions where you pursued or obtained a previous degree (must be received before the national application deadline)
Unofficial transcripts must include your name, the name of the institution, titles of the courses, and the grades obtained
Description of the study abroad program: a screenshot or PDF from the program's website, or a scanned program brochure, limited to no more than 5 pages
Two letters of recommendation (third optional) for Boren Scholarships, submitted by the recommenders through the online application system
Three letters of recommendation for Boren Fellowships, submitted by the recommenders through the online application system
Optional language proficiency evaluation completed by a language instructor, which does not count toward the Letters of Recommendation requirement
Optional letter of affiliation from an overseas host institution or faculty (Boren Fellowship applicants only)
application_method: Visit the Apply Now page and select the overseas location and language you want to study
Reach out to your Boren Awards campus representative at your institution for advice (you may still apply if your institution does not have one)
Watch the introductory webinar and review the official selection criteria
Choose a programme: apply for a Regional Flagship Language Initiative or select/design your own study programme
Complete and review the essays with your recommenders
Submit the application through the online application system by the national deadline
existing.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated by IIE-organized regional merit review panels made up of faculty members and administrators from colleges and universities across the United States, representing a wide array of fields of study. The panels make recommendations on each submitted, eligible application, with final decision-making authority held by the program's federal sponsor, DLNSEO. There is no semi-finalist or interview phase, so everything an applicant would want the selection committee to know must be stated in the essays and other application materials. Selection preference is given to veterans when other factors are equivalent.
existing.best_fit: U.S. citizens aged 18 or over who are matriculated at an accredited U.S. undergraduate or graduate degree programme, can commit 8-52 weeks to overseas study of a Boren-preferred language in a Boren-preferred region, and intend to pursue a federal national-security career.
existing.notes: Non-deferrable in practice: recipients must remain matriculated at their U.S. institution for the whole funded period and may not graduate until the award is complete, and overseas programmes must be approved by a Boren Program Advisor before travel. Not renewable as published - the award is a fixed one-time grant tier set by overseas duration, and requests to increase awards above the published maximums are contingent upon availability of funds. No return-home obligation is published; instead recipients must complete at least one year of federal service in support of U.S. national security after graduation, with preference given to a longer-term commitment. Internships conducted during a Boren-funded period may not be remunerated nor conducted with the U.S. or a foreign government, and Boren Fellows may not work as journalists while abroad, even freelance or unpaid. Funding for programme expenses incurred after May 31, 2028 is contingent upon availability and cannot be guaranteed at the time of award.
existing.duration: 8 to 52 weeks of overseas study; 25-52 weeks preferred; minimum 12 weeks for most applicants (8 weeks minimum for undergraduate STEM summer programmes).
existing.application_period: The 2027-2028 Boren Scholarship and Boren Fellowship application cycle is open as of 2026-10-01. National deadlines are January 20, 2027 (Fellowships) and January 27, 2027 (Scholarships), 5pm Eastern time. Selected applicants are notified in mid-to-late April. Campus representatives may set earlier campus deadlines that applicants are asked to respect.
existing.deadline_display: National deadlines for the 2027 Boren Awards: Boren Fellowships January 20, 2027; Boren Scholarships January 27, 2027 - both 5pm Eastern time.
